title: Algebraic and formal conormal complexes resolve completed differentials
statement:
Let $k$ be a perfect field and $S$ a reduced finite-type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], pure of dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-pure-dimension] and a local complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Let $\mathfrak m$ be a maximal ideal with residue field $k$, $A=S_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and $R=\widehat A$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], assumed reduced. Choose $A=P/I$, where $P=k[u_1,\ldots,u_m]_{\mathfrak q}$ at a $k$-rational maximal ideal and $I=(h_1,\ldots,h_{m-d})$ is generated by a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Let $\pi:T=k[[z_1,\ldots,z_n]]\twoheadrightarrow R$ be a continuous local $k$-algebra surjection [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] with kernel $J=(g_1,\ldots,g_c)$ a regular sequence in $(z)$ and $n-c=d$. Put $N=\Omega^1_{A/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and $M_R=N\otimes_A R$ [def-weil-module-base-change]. Then $S,A,R$ are Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $A\to R$ is faithfully flat (flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] with surjective map of spectra), and $N$ is finite, generated by the images of $\mathrm du_i$. The universal derivation extends uniquely to a continuous $k$-derivation $\widehat d:R\to M_R$ [def-trf-completed-differential-extension]. There are exact sequences
$$0\to (I/I^2)\otimes_A R\xrightarrow{\mathrm d}(\Omega^1_{P/k}\otimes_P A)\otimes_A R\xrightarrow{q_P} M_R\to0,$$
$$0\to J/J^2\xrightarrow{\widehat{\mathrm d}}R^n\xrightarrow{q_T}M_R\to0,$$
where $q_P(\mathrm du_i\otimes1)=\mathrm d(\bar u_i)\otimes1$, $\widehat{\mathrm d}[g]=(\pi(\partial g/\partial z_i))_i$, and $q_T(e_i)=\widehat d(\pi(z_i))$. The four left-hand terms are finite free of ranks $m-d,m,c,n$, respectively, with the indicated equation and coordinate bases. Thus the two-term complexes in degrees $-1,0$ augment quasi-isomorphically to $M_R[0]$ in the derived category on $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-pc-derived-category]. For any field $L$ and $k$-algebra map $R\to L$ whose restriction to $A$ factors through a generic point in its smooth $d$-dimensional locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], both displayed sequences remain short exact after tensoring over $R$ with $L$, with common cokernel $N\otimes_A L$ of dimension $d$; no flatness of $R\to L$ is assumed.

source.place: Agent-formulated common-resolution consequence of Tags 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular), 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring), 00RT (lemma-differentials-localize), 00RU (lemma-differential-seq), 00MC (lemma-completion-faithfully-flat), 02LX (lemma-total-ring-fractions-no-embedded-points); varieties.tex Tag 0C52 (lemma-complete-local-ring-structure-as-algebra) motivates the continuous presentation. Returned parent proof Steps 1--2, 5 and 9, using the generic-rank input of Steps 3--4. These sources do not state the entire auxiliary assertion verbatim.

proof.text: A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$. Apply finite-type Noetherian permanence to $k\to S$, localization permanence to $S\to A$, and Noetherian completion to $A\to R$. This proves the three Noetherian assertions. The local-completion faithful-flatness theorem applies to the Noetherian local ring $A$ and its maximal-ideal completion, giving both flatness and surjectivity on spectra.

The polynomial differential basis, followed by differential localization at $\mathfrak q$, identifies $\Omega^1_{P/k}$ with $P^m$ on $\mathrm du_i$. The regular-sequence conormal theorem applied in $P$ and in $T$ identifies $I/I^2$ with $A^{m-d}$ on $[h_j]$ and $J/J^2$ with $R^c$ on $[g_j]$. Tensoring the first two bases gives the required ranks $m-d,m$ over $R$; the formal middle term is already $R^n$ on $e_i$. Explicitly the base-changed basis isomorphism is $(\sum a_i b_i)\otimes r\mapsto(a_i r)_i$, with inverse $(r_i)_i\mapsto\sum b_i\otimes r_i$.

Apply the quotient differential sequence to $k\to P\twoheadrightarrow A=P/I$. It gives $I/I^2\to\Omega^1_{P/k}\otimes_P A\to N\to0$ with $[h]\mapsto\mathrm dh\otimes1$ and $\mathrm du_i\otimes1\mapsto\mathrm d\bar u_i$. In particular $N$ is generated by the $m$ indicated coordinate differentials and is finite. Tensor right exactness with $R$ gives the first displayed row, except for injectivity at its left end, with exactly the stipulated map $q_P$. This use of right exactness requires no flatness.

Use the completion differential comparison with residue extension $F=k$ and section the given structural map $k\to R$. The extension is finite separable (the identity), so this gives existence and uniqueness of the continuous extension $\widehat d:R\to N\otimes_A R$. Apply the completed Jacobian differential theorem to the specified continuous surjection $T\twoheadrightarrow R$, with its kernel generators $g_1,\ldots,g_c$. It identifies the cokernel of $R^c\to R^n$, $(a_j)\mapsto(\sum_j a_j\pi(\partial_i g_j))_i$, with $M_R$, sending $e_i$ to $\widehat d(\pi(z_i))$. Under the conormal basis of Step 2 this first arrow is precisely the asserted map on $J/J^2$. For any $g=\sum a_jg_j\in J$, the derivation rule modulo $J$ gives $\pi(\partial_i g)=\sum_j\pi(a_j)\pi(\partial_i g_j)$; derivatives of elements of $J^2$ vanish modulo $J$. Thus the formula on arbitrary classes $[g]$ is well-defined and agrees with that arrow. The second displayed row is right exact.

source.place: Continuous extension and completed Jacobian cokernel, applied with the identity residue extension; elementary conormal generator calculation

proof.text: Let $L$ be a field with one of the allowed maps $R\to L$. By the generic completed differential rank theorem, $N\otimes_A L$ has dimension $d$. Tensor right exactness applied to the two rows of Steps 3--4 gives right exact sequences $L^a\xrightarrow{D}L^b\xrightarrow{q}N\otimes_A L\to0$, where $(a,b)=(m-d,m)$ or $(c,n)$, so $b-a=d$ in either case. Rank-nullity for the surjective $q$ gives $\dim\ker q=b-d=a$. Exactness gives $\operatorname{im}D=\ker q$, hence rank-nullity for $D$ gives $\dim\ker D=a-a=0$ and $D$ is injective. This proves the full final assertion, including the specified common cokernel and its dimension. The same argument applies to every minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$ with $L=R_{\mathfrak p}$: the generic rank theorem supplies that this is a field, that its contraction in $A$ is minimal and smooth of dimension $d$, and that the completed differential fibre has dimension $d$.

source.place: Generic rank input and tensor right exactness; rank-nullity applied to each of the two finite-dimensional maps

proof.text: Both left arrows over $R$ are now injective. Indeed take a kernel vector $v$ in either of their free source modules, in the bases of Step 2. Its image in $R_{\mathfrak p}^{a}$ is zero for every minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ by Step 5. The reduced-Noetherian total-fractions theorem applies because $R$ is reduced by hypothesis and Noetherian by Step 1; it identifies $Q(R)$ with the product of these fields. Every coordinate of $v$ therefore maps to zero in $Q(R)$. By the definition of localization, a coordinate $x$ mapping to zero is killed by a nonzerodivisor $s\in R$; $sx=0$ and the defining property of $s$ give $x=0$. Thus $v=0$. Together with Steps 3--4 this establishes the two short exact sequences over $R$.

source.place: Tag 02LX (lemma-total-ring-fractions-no-embedded-points), applied to a reduced Noetherian ring; elementary coordinatewise localization argument

proof.text: The associated-sheaf functor on $\operatorname{Spec}R$ preserves finite limits by the tilde finite-limit theorem and all small colimits by the affine tilde/Gamma theorem. It therefore carries the two short exact module sequences to short exact sequences of module sheaves: kernels are finite limits and cokernels are finite colimits. For either associated two-term complex $C$, its augmentation $C\to\widetilde{M_R}[0]$ has $H^{-1}(C)=\ker D=0$ and $H^0(C)=\operatorname{coker}D=\widetilde{M_R}$ via the specified $q$; all other cohomology objects vanish because the complex is concentrated in degrees $-1,0$. By the definition of quasi-isomorphism this augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism and hence becomes invertible in the derived category of module sheaves. This is the derived-category assertion in the statement.

source.place: Tags 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), 01ID (lemma-colimit-quasi-coherent); definition of cohomology and quasi-isomorphism
